executiveSummary:
Actuals are closed through January 2026, while several quarterly and trailing visuals reflect the latest closed quarter of December 2025. Sections covering recent ARR transactions and budget performance explicitly include January 2026 actuals. Overall, the business closed Dec 25 at £9.4M ARR with strong growth and healthy unit economics; January activity lifted total ARR to £9.69M per the ARR composition views. Profitability remains slightly negative on an EBIT/EBITDA basis, with efficiency metrics indicating room to trade spend between growth and retention.

What is proven by actuals to Jan 26: rapid ARR growth (TTM c.70% at Dec 25), high gross margin (~78%), strong payback and unit economics (CAC ~0.56; LTV:CAC ~6.5), but sub-benchmark retention (logo ~85%, gross ~79%, NRR ~90% improving to ~92% in Jan 26). The FY25 plan was exceeded on ARR (+11%) and EBITDA modestly outperformed; Jan 26 EBITDA beat monthly budget by ~34%.

What is expected in the forecast beyond Dec 25/Jan 26: ARR expansion to mid–high teens by Dec 27 assumes higher logo adds, improved net retention (frequent ≥100% in out-quarters), and operating leverage as headcount scales from 64 to >100. These are assumptions, not yet evidenced.

  • Retention and expansion quality: Actual GRR/NRR remain below typical SaaS benchmarks; the forecast assumes improvement. Focus on cohort diagnostics, save/expand playbooks, pricing/packaging, and success coverage in at-risk segments.
  • Path to profitability while sustaining growth: EBIT is still negative; the model assumes leverage as hiring rises. Focus on quota capacity and payback discipline, mix-shifting spend toward proven channels, and guardrails on G&A.
  • Deal mix and concentration: Growth is weighted to new logos (last 12 months) with concentration in Energy & Utilities and selected regions. Focus on diversification thresholds, enterprise expansion motions, and exposure limits by vertical/region.
page1:
The dashboard (quarterly/trailing view through Dec 25) shows £9.4M ARR, ~70% ARR growth, and strong unit economics (CAC ~0.56, LTV:CAC ~6.5). Gross margin is ~78% and recurring revenue mix is ~94%. Offsets are sub-benchmark retention (logo ~85%, gross ~79%, NRR ~90%) and negative EBIT (~-7%). This combination supports continued investment capacity, but the retention drag is the primary constraint on durable growth.

Interpretation in the context of forecast: efficiency metrics are observed; any further improvement is assumed in the plan and not yet evidenced. The Rule of 40 at ~63% reflects high growth despite negative EBIT; sustaining this will depend on retention lift and disciplined spend as hiring scales.

No new management focus items identified on this page.
page2:
The ARR and deals table confirms actuals through Dec 25: 8 new and 4 lost logos in the quarter; logo retention ~84%, gross retention ~81%, and net retention ~91%. ARR ended Dec 25 at £9.42M with quarterly net ARR of ~£0.51M and 25% quarterly growth from the base. Beyond Dec 25, the forecast assumes rising logo additions, higher net retention (often ≥100%), and ARR compounding to ~£17.6M by Dec 27.

Implication: the forward plan relies on a step-up in retention and continued new logo velocity. Given current retention is below benchmark, the improvement embedded in the forecast is a material execution assumption.

Management focus reinforcement: Retention and expansion quality. Prioritise cohort and use-case level churn diagnostics, standardized renewal health scoring, pricing/packaging checks, and targeted expansion plays to close the gap between actual NRR (~90–92%) and the forecasted levels.
page3:
P&L through Dec 25 shows revenue of ~£2.61M for the quarter, gross margin ~78%, and operating cost mix of S&M ~31%, Development ~28%, and G&A ~16%. EBIT for the quarter was ~-£53k, consistent with the dashboard EBIT profile. Headcount closed Dec 25 at 64. The forward view scales headcount toward ~106 by Dec 27, while EBIT turns positive in 2026/27 in the model—this is forecast, not yet reflected in actual run-rate.

Interpretation: Gross margin provides room for operating leverage, but breakeven requires either higher NRR/expansion or tighter overhead efficiency as hiring increases. The assumed improvement in EBIT depends on maintaining CAC/payback discipline while adding quota capacity.

Management focus reinforcement: Path to profitability while sustaining growth. Emphasise productivity guardrails (quota attainment, pipeline coverage), payback by channel, and G&A spending controls to convert gross margin into EBIT as scale increases.
page4:
ARR composition incorporates Jan 26 actuals. Total ARR reached ~£9.69M, with Energy & Utilities (~£3.99M) and Life Science (~£2.50M) the largest verticals; by region, South America (~£2.32M), Asia (~£2.09M), Africa (~£1.95M), North America (~£1.91M), and Europe (~£1.42M) indicate a relatively diversified footprint. The 12‑month waterfall from a £5.81M base shows growth primarily from new lands (~£4.32M) and more modest expansion (~£0.71M), offset by downsell (~£0.27M) and logo loss (~£0.88M). NRR on a rolling basis dipped to ~90% late 2025 and ticked up to ~92% in Jan 26—improving but still sub‑100%.

Implication: growth has been new‑logo led; durability depends on lifting expansion and reducing churn. Concentration in one to two verticals underscores the value of deepening cross‑sell/upsell motions within existing accounts to stabilise NRR.

Management focus reinforcement: Retention and expansion quality. Focus on post‑land adoption metrics, packaged add‑ons, and success coverage in the largest verticals/regions to convert new‑logo momentum into durable NRR.
page5:
The last‑3‑months transactions (actuals for Nov 25, Dec 25, and Jan 26) total ~£855k ARR: ~£720k from 8 new logos, ~£180k from 4 expansions, and ~£45k of downsell. By industry, Energy & Utilities (~£360k new) and Government (~£270k new) led; by region, South America and Africa were strongest contributors to new ARR. Customer‑level detail shows breadth rather than a single outsized deal, with limited downsell activity in the period.

Implication: early‑Q1 momentum remains new‑logo driven with healthy geographic spread and modest expansion. This is positive for near‑term growth but reinforces the need to strengthen expansion velocity to improve NRR.

No new management focus items identified on this page.
page6:
Budget analysis includes Jan 26 actuals alongside FY25 actuals. For FY25 (to Dec 25), revenue was ~1% above budget, gross margin ~1% below, and EBITDA outperformed by ~£30k (5%). Mix-wise, S&M was under budget (~+12% variance favorable), Development slightly over (~-3%), and G&A materially over (~-38%). Quarterly Q4’25 EBITDA beat budget by ~£76k (59%). January 2026 (monthly) also beat EBITDA budget by ~£18k (34%). On ARR, FY25 delivered +11% versus plan, driven by higher additions (+£329k) and lower attrition (+£115k) despite slightly lower upsell and higher downsell versus budget.

Implication: execution exceeded the top‑line and ARR plans with disciplined S&M spend, but G&A over‑run diluted operating leverage. The 2026 forecast assumes continued EBITDA improvement; sustaining beats will require keeping G&A in check while ensuring S&M capacity is sufficient to meet the higher ARR targets.

Management focus reinforcement: Path to profitability while sustaining growth. Tighten G&A governance (run‑rate reviews, vendor rationalisation, zero‑based budgeting where appropriate) and validate S&M capacity against pipeline coverage so that budget favourability does not constrain the forecasted ARR trajectory.
